beats: Hook: a GPU is thousands of workers who can only march in squads of 32 (line_gpu_squad_march).
CPU vs GPU: a few master chefs (line_d_chefs) vs a hall full of identical line cooks; the GPU is a kitchen inside the box (line_pc_kitchen, line_gpu).

Architecture: many SMs = identical cooking stations sharing one big pantry (DRAM) and one long shared counter (L2) (line_gpu_kitchen_hall); one station up close: own burners (functional units), own boards (registers), own small shelf (on-chip cache) (line_gpu_station).

Kernel, grid, block, thread: one recipe card for everyone, the order is a rail of tickets (the grid), each ticket (block) goes to one station (SM), the manager (host CPU) pins the recipe and walks off: launch is asynchronous (line_gpu_ticket_rail).
Warps: cooks move in squads of 32 in lockstep (SIMT); an if/else makes half the squad wait while the other half works, then swap (line_gpu_warp_branch).

The memory ladder: in your hand (registers), the team's counter (shared memory), the pantry down the hall (global memory: HBM + L2), the warehouse across town (host memory): smaller but faster the closer it is (line_gpu_memory_reach).
Pitfall: fetching one carrot per trip leaves the squad idle (line_gpu_pantry_trek); fast code brings a whole tray to the counter once (line_gpu_tray_fetch).

Vector addition end to end: allocate, copy in by truck, launch, copy back (the manager waits at the dock: implicit sync), free (line_gpu_truck_dock); the kernel itself: every cook adds one small bowl into one big bowl at the same moment, y[i] += x[i] (line_gpu_bowl_row).
Cliffhanger: so many models times so many chips is too many kernels to write by hand (line_kernel_pile_coder from L09-02's plan, or line_heap).
Cover (line_cover_l09_01; for the X post and thumbnails, not a film beat): thirty-two identical line cooks march in lockstep, four rows of eight.
